sections.overview: This Indo-Pacific cone snail is a predatory marine gastropod in family Conidae, whose members hunt with venomous radular teeth.
sections.identification: Its conical, patterned shell can resemble that of Conus consors, and shell appearance alone may not reliably separate them.
sections.habitat: It lives in shallow Indo-Pacific waters; museum specimens have been collected on sandy reef substrate in Indonesia.
sections.diet: Juveniles hunt polychaete worms, then shift to fish as adults, using a hooked radular tooth and paralytic venom peptides.
sections.behavior: It injects venom through a hollow radular tooth; research documents different hunting behavior and venom mixtures in juveniles and adults.
sections.reproduction: Females deposit egg capsules on hard surfaces, and laboratory-reared larvae swim and feed before settling and metamorphosing.
sections.ecology: It is the type species of subgenus Pionoconus; adults hunt fish, while juveniles retain a worm-eating phase.
sections.conservation: The French SeaLifeBase record provides no verified global threat category, so this profile assigns none.
